root_cause.text: The ntfs3 compressed-read path acquired the inode mutex `ni_lock` too early in `ntfs_read_folio()`, before locking all folios/pages in the compressed frame, creating an ABBA lock inversion with page locks in `ni_read_folio_cmpr()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `ni_lock(ni)`/`ni_unlock(ni)` from `ntfs_read_folio()` in `fs/ntfs3/inode.c` and moves `ni_lock(ni)` into `ni_read_folio_cmpr()` in `fs/ntfs3/frecord.c` after the page array has been collected, matching the commit note that the deadlock was due to `Task A` holding `ni_lock` while waiting on page `Y` and `Task B` holding page `Y` while waiting on `ni_lock`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Protect ni_read_frame() with inode locking to fix a race during compressed folio reads.
intent_record.what: The code adds a call to ni_lock(ni) immediately before ni_read_frame(ni, frame_vbo, pages, pages_per_frame, 0) and adds a matching ni_unlock(ni) immediately after that call.
intent_record.how: This serializes access to the ntfs inode state while reading a compressed frame, preventing concurrent modifications or races during the ni_read_frame() operation and ensuring the frame read runs under the inode lock.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix compressed NTFS folio reads to acquire `ni_lock` inside `ni_read_folio_cmpr` instead of in the caller.
intent_record.what: In `ntfs_read_folio()`, the explicit `ni_lock(ni)` before calling `ni_read_folio_cmpr(ni, folio)` was removed, along with the matching `ni_unlock(ni)` after the call. A comment was added stating that `ni_lock` is acquired inside `ni_read_folio_cmpr` after page locks.
intent_record.how: This changes the locking flow so the compressed-folio read path no longer double-locks the inode state from the caller. Runtime behavior is preserved or corrected by delegating lock acquisition to `ni_read_folio_cmpr`, which avoids an incorrect lock ordering or redundant lock nesting and relies on the callee to manage the lock at the proper point.

The vulnerable construct is present at lines 697-701: `if (is_compressed(ni)) { ni_lock(ni); err = ni_readpage_cmpr(ni, page); ni_unlock(ni); return err; }`. This acquires `ni_lock` before calling the compressed-page reader, which matches the root cause description that `ni_lock` was taken too early in `ntfs_read_folio()`/compressed read path and could invert lock order with page locks in `ni_read_folio_cmpr()`.
